newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close softer, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close softer, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates continued their recent downturn to finish lower on Friday as local banks liquidiated excess funds amid loose liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.362 percent against Thursday's 5.402 close, with the 30-day commercial paper at 5.25 against 5.30.

Dealers attributed falls in the money rates partly to the Taiwan dollar's recent appreciation. Many players had rushed to sell their U.S. dollar positions because of the rising local currency, they said.
The Taiwan dollar finished weaker at T$27.391 on Friday.
Liquidity demand for the Chinese New Year, which falls on February 7, is expected to gradually increase next week, dealers added.
Government bond yields hovered in low levels after the auction of T$40 billion government bonds at an average yield of 6.2650 percent in the afternoon.
The 15-year bond yield was traded at 6.255-250. Traders were mixed about the bond market's outlooks.
